spec.instruction: The toilet is clogged. Deal with it safely.
spec.notes: Bowl/tank/clog state machine (toilets.py). Ordinary paper clog: 20 flange strokes clear it, the flush test siphons. spec.instruction: Report damaged latch.
spec.notes: Realistic perception: a gate resting shut looks latched at a glance (latched is inspect-tier). A close, lit inspection shows the seeded fault's evidence - a bent bar, a missing keeper screw, or the latch bar sitting below the catch (an eyeballed gap, 5 mm resolution) - and what it points to. The report must name the hidden fault and reach the resident; a sagging gate can and should be latched by lifting it, the other faults cannot latch (left shut). Tier 1: the reference walks up to the gate from the yard side (mechanisms.approach no longer opens the gate on the way through) and shuts it only when it stands open (mechanisms.shut: the wind may have blown it open or not, held-out seed 701 starts it shut). Camera: verified with the geometric camera; the across-the-yard look is the camera wrong plan (the latch hardware needs a close look within reach). Generation 1 (M-GEN2): on generation-2 houses (seed 97) outdoor_plants' wind blows both patio chairs onto the patio's doorway cell to the backyard, which leaves no route to the gate (cross-domain bug reported to outdoor_plants); the spec moves to generation 2 once that is fixed.
phrasings: Report damaged latch.
The side gate latch seems off - check it and let me know what's wrong.

spec.instruction: Check the trash levels: how full are the kitchen trash can and the recycling bin? Tell me each as a fraction of full.
spec.notes: Realistic perception: fill_level is rendered as a glance bucket (FILL5) until the bin is inspected, then to 5 % with viewpoint noise; the reference reports what it observed after opening and inspecting (the perceivability check sees the reported numbers in its observations). Levels sit near the edges of the 'half' bucket, so neither the bucket word nor its middle is within 0.12. Geometric camera: the reference looks into each bin with the wrist (inspect where=inside, which records camera_log.looked_in) and success needs both looks; the camera wrong plan crouches below the rims and inspects without looking in. Kernel gap (reported): a geometric inspect still renders an open bin's fill_level without a look inside, so that plan's numbers are right and only the missing looks fail it. camera_log is written only by the geometric camera, so this spec is geometric-only. Phase 1 (2026-10-22): the first wrong plan used to read a glance bucket before any inspection, which the geometric camera never shows (a closed can, an open-top bin from beside it), so it raised before its mistake and the hardened verifier no longer counts it; it now inspects each bin from where it stands and reports the level that shows, and fails on the missing look into the recycling bin.
phrasings: Check the trash levels: how full are the kitchen trash can and the recycling bin? Tell me each as a fraction of full.
How full are the kitchen bin and the recycling bin? Give me a fraction for each.
Do a trash check - report how full the kitchen can and the recycling are.
spec.title: Check how full the kitchen can and the recycling bin are and report each level

spec.instruction: How much does the {item_label} weigh? Use the kitchen scale and tell me in grams.
spec.notes: Realistic perception: a glance or an inspection gives only a visual estimate (about +-15 %, two significant figures: inspect food_view.approx_g; holding it gives light/medium/heavy). The scale's display is the measurement (weigh grants read of the display and measure of the item's mass). The scale starts off and in ounces: switching it on zeroes it with whatever is on the platform, so it must be switched on (and set to grams) before the item goes on. The reported value must equal the display (the verifier also checks that the number appeared in what the robot observed). Generation-2 house; passes with the geometric camera (realistic default after the D3 switch-over).
phrasings: Weigh.

spec.instruction: The wind keeps lifting the papers on the patio table. Find something heavy enough to hold them down.
spec.notes: Perception is the skill. Realistic mode: a solid river stone (1.4 kg) and a hollow resin replica (0.15 kg) are the look-alike group smooth_stone (resolve never: no look, however close, tells them apart); which of the two spawn slots holds the real one alternates by variant. Mass is a measure-tier field: support mode=heft (or lifting it) grants touch and reports a light/medium/heavy impression, never the number. The papers lift at 3 m/s unless at least hold_down_kg = 0.5 kg rests on them; the wind rises to 6.5 m/s with a 7.5 m/s gust at 300 s (manipulation.wind / manipulation.gust). The setup pins the morning's gusts at 2.5 m/s (a generation-2 day draws its own gust_mps, 7.1 m/s on seed 0, which would lift the papers before the robot acts; the kernel wind law's default gust is 1.5 x the mean). The reference waits 420 s on its own clock (agent-legal). Wrong plans act on looks (the first stone, a solid-looking mug) or ignore what the heft said.

spec.instruction: Find something soft to protect this vase for the move, then pack it in the moving box and close it.
spec.notes: Perception is the skill. Realistic mode: a bubble wrap roll and a roll of moving stretch film are the look-alike group clear_plastic_roll ('roll of clear plastic film', resolved by inspect: the bubbles are visible up close); which spawn slot holds which alternates by variant. Closing the box with the vase inside triggers a 0.76 m transport drop (ISTA 1A for a parcel under 10 kg), taken through the kernel's impact: the glass vase (drop tolerance 0.3 m, +-15 % per instance) feels 0.76 m / its padding factor (1 + padding/3 mm; an unstuffed hollow piece counts half its padding): 2 layers of bubble wrap, stuffed (9.6 mm, factor 4.2) -> 0.18 m, survives; one unstuffed layer (4.8 mm counted 2.4, factor 1.8) -> 0.42 m, kraft paper (1 mm, 1.33) -> 0.57 m and stretch film (0 mm) -> 0.76 m break. The box is pre-filled with crumpled paper so voids stay under 20 %. Wrong plans act on glance-level belief (first clear roll), on 'paper is padding', or ignore what the close look showed. Geometric camera (looking is the skill): the bubbles show only to a close look with the cameras on (the reference approaches the table and inspects both rolls); the camera wrong plan only aims its head at the rolls from where it stands (a look gives the glance tier: two rolls of clear film) and guesses the film.

spec.instruction: Dry this without shrinking it.
spec.notes: Variants: wool sweater (dry flat, ~1.5 days), cotton tee labelled tumble-low (low-heat sensor cycle), rayon dress (line dry). High heat beyond the label shrinks/felts; bunched damp laundry sours. Residents 'minimal': the wool variant dries for ~1.5 days and ends at night; residents sleep at night and switch lights at dusk and in the morning (people domain), so the long wait raises no unrelated failure. Waits (tier-1 sweep, M-WAITS): the plans no longer poll the garment's hidden wetness; the flat-dried sweater is felt every 4 h for 56 h (it dries in 34-49 h on the verification seeds), the hung dress every hour for 4 h (2-3 h), and the dryer variant listens for the dryer's end buzzer (textiles_laundry.wait_cycle: wait interrupt_on appliance_done). Phase 1 (hashed variants put the sweater on seed 1, whose rack stands in a windowless laundry room): the feel checks go through textiles_laundry.feel_garment, which switches the room light on for a check that falls at night and off again (a bare inspect is refused in the dark).

spec.instruction: Please go to the {goal_room}. Watch out - this room has floor-to-ceiling glass and mirrors that can look like openings.
spec.notes: Realistic perception shows a mirror or reflective glass panel as an open doorway until it is inspected; until then the planner has no glass margin to route around (navigation_robot masks it), so avoid=['glass'] alone does not help. Walking into it is a collision (global harm) and cracks the panel at walking pace. Geometric camera (tier 1): telling the panel from an opening is a close look with the cameras on; the camera wrong plan keeps them off (privacy mode), so only the depth sensors answer, and they are fooled by glass and mirrors.
